- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to align with mean-reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots in subsequent days; cap forecast at +3% above peak or use 20-day moving average for smoothing.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, apply downward correction proportional to sentiment decay (e.g., 0.5x sentiment weight).
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >3% from 18-day moving average, adjust forecast to align with recent sentiment trend (e.g., if sentiment rising, forecast upward; if falling, downward).
- When sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows, model exhibits lag; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead if sentiment is trending upward, or delay if trending downward.
